# War Scroll Column 7 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 1QM (Cave 1), Col. 7 | **Condition:** complete

---

**1** No boy or woman may enter the war camps from the time the army marches out of Jerusalem until it returns.

**2** No one who is lame, blind, crippled, or bearing any permanent physical defect, and no one suffering from any bodily impurity,

**3** may go out with them to battle. Every soldier must be a willing volunteer, sound in mind and body, ready for the Day of God's Vengeance.

**4** Any man who has had a seminal emission and is not yet ritually clean on the day of battle must stay behind, because God's holy angels march in the ranks alongside the soldiers.

**5** The camp latrine must be at least two thousand cubits from any camp, and no nakedness may be exposed anywhere near the camps.

**6** When the army deploys for battle, the soldiers arrange themselves in their encampments, each man taking his assigned position, standing watch with weapons in hand.

**7** Armed escorts go out to handle camp necessities and stand guard constantly over the entire camp perimeter, so that nothing defiles the sacred space of the encampments.

**8** Sentries man their posts around the camps, and night watchmen keep their shifts — no one lays down his weapon.

**9** Any man who needs to relieve himself goes out armed, and the escort accompanies him until he returns to camp.

**10** When the battle lines form up, three rows of cavalry take position on each side of the formation.

**11** The rows are spaced a hundred cubits apart, with fifty cubits between each rank, all standing in formation facing the enemy.

**12** Each cavalry row has a hundred horsemen, arranged on the flanks of the battle line — seven hundred riders on each side.

**13** They fan out to the right and left of the main line to terrify the enemies of God and cut off anyone who tries to flee.

**14** Infantry soldiers must be between forty and fifty years old; camp officers between fifty and sixty.

**15** Cavalry riders must be between thirty and forty-five. Those assigned to strip the dead, gather the spoils, and purify the battlefield

**16** must be between twenty-five and thirty. No young man may go out to fight on the day of battle.

**17** All of these must be willing volunteers for God's war — intelligent, capable men who serve according to the structure of their assigned units.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Column 7's purity rules are rooted in Deuteronomy 23:10-15 but intensified for eschatological holy war. The rationale — angels march with the army (7:4) — is the key theological claim. "Place of the hand" (Hebrew euphemism for latrine) rendered directly. Age requirements reveal a sophisticated military organization with distinct roles for different age groups.*
